boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Saint Mary’s College rituals, landmarks, and annual milestones.

cards.title: Close the Circle
cards.subtitle: First-year orientation tradition
cards.notes: During orientation, join your incoming class for this ceremonial gathering that marks the beginning of its shared Saint Mary’s experience.
cards.short_summary: A first-year class ritual held during orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s identifies Closing the Circle as an orientation event for first-year students that signifies coming together as a class.
cards.access_notes: Participation is part of incoming-student orientation; confirm orientation details with the College.

cards.title: Open the Circle
cards.subtitle: Senior Week tradition
cards.notes: See the senior class revisit the circle during Senior Week, using the ceremony to mark departure from the College community.
cards.short_summary: A Senior Week counterpart to the first-year circle ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s states that seniors attend Opening the Circle during Senior Week as a symbol of leaving the College to make a difference in the world.
cards.access_notes: For graduating seniors during Senior Week; consult College communications for program details.

cards.title: Take the First Walk
cards.subtitle: Orientation on The Avenue
cards.notes: At orientation, walk The Avenue with your class while family and friends cheer the first official passage through this campus landmark.
cards.short_summary: New students’ ceremonial first trip down The Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says family and friends cheer students during their first official walk down The Avenue at Orientation.
cards.access_notes: An orientation activity for incoming students; follow the College’s orientation schedule.

cards.title: Make the Last Walk
cards.subtitle: Senior Week on The Avenue
cards.notes: During Senior Week, follow the mirrored route down The Avenue as faculty and staff cheer the class through its final campus walk.
cards.short_summary: Graduating students’ final ceremonial walk down The Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s documents a final walk down The Avenue during Senior Week, with faculty and staff cheering students on.
cards.access_notes: For graduating seniors during Senior Week; follow the College’s published schedule.

cards.title: Wear the Saint Mary’s Ring
cards.subtitle: Junior-year class-ring tradition
cards.notes: If you choose to purchase one in junior year, look closely at the Ring’s Spes Unica motto, French cross, and Holy Cross anchors.
cards.short_summary: The College’s distinctive class ring links Belles across generations.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says juniors may purchase its class ring, whose design includes Spes Unica, the French cross, and anchors from Holy Cross and College seals.
cards.access_notes: Optional junior-year purchase; obtain current ordering and pricing details directly from the College.

cards.title: Climb the Bell Tower
cards.subtitle: Le Mans Hall; Senior Week and Reunion
cards.notes: Plan for the limited Bell Tower tour window offered in Senior Week, then return for a Reunion visit when the tower opens again.
cards.short_summary: A landmark tower visit reserved for Senior Week and Reunion.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s states that students tour the Bell Tower during Senior Week and when they return for Reunion.
cards.access_notes: Tours are limited to Senior Week and Reunion periods according to the College; verify availability before planning.

cards.title: Stay for Senior Week
cards.subtitle: The week before Commencement
cards.notes: For graduating students, use the week before Commencement to take part in the College’s planned class activities and milestone ceremonies.
cards.short_summary: A full pre-Commencement week reserved for graduating seniors.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s describes Senior Week as a full week of activities for seniors after other students leave campus and before Commencement.
cards.access_notes: For graduating seniors immediately before Commencement; activity details vary by year.

cards.title: Leave a Handprint
cards.subtitle: Senior Week tunnel tradition
cards.notes: During Senior Week, add your handprint only through the College-organized class opportunity, contributing to the designated tunnel section with classmates.
cards.short_summary: A class handprint ritual that marks seniors’ contribution to Saint Mary’s.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says each class can fill a tunnel section with handprints during Senior Week as a symbol of having a hand in shaping the College.
cards.access_notes: Participate only through the Senior Week class activity and in the section designated by the College.

cards.title: Attend a Madrigal Dinner
cards.subtitle: Annual Department of Music holiday event
cards.notes: Attend the annual Renaissance-style holiday dinner and performance, where courses are announced with fanfare and song amid seasonal entertainment.
cards.short_summary: A Saint Mary’s Christmas banquet-performance tradition dating to 1972.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says its Department of Music has presented an annual Christmas Madrigal Dinner since 1972, with a Renaissance-style banquet and performance.
cards.access_notes: Annual event; consult the Department of Music or College events calendar for current tickets and timing.

cards.title: Mark Founders’ Day
cards.subtitle: October 13 College observance
cards.notes: Use the October observance to learn about Father Sorin, Mother Angela Gillespie, and Basil Moreau, figures central to Saint Mary’s founding.
cards.short_summary: An annual observance of Saint Mary’s founding and its co-founders.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s style guidance states that Founders’ Day is traditionally celebrated October 13 and honors Father Edward Sorin, Mother Angela Gillespie, and Blessed Basil Anthony Moreau.
cards.access_notes: Traditionally observed October 13; check College announcements for any current campus programming.
